question: In the year 1904, who formed a secret organisation of revolutionaries named Abhinav Bharat?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinayak Damodar Savarkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, also known as Veer Savarkar, was an Indian independence activist, lawyer, and writer.
 
• In 1904, he founded a secret society of revolutionaries called Abhinav Bharat Society in Pune, Maharashtra.
 
• The main objective of Abhinav Bharat was to create a network of young revolutionaries committed to the cause of Indian independence.
 
• Abhinav Bharat played a significant role in inspiring other revolutionary groups and activities against the British colonial rule in India.
 
• Vinayak Damodar Savarkar was also a key figure in the Hindu nationalist movement and authored several works on Indian history and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolutionary Activities:**

 
 
• Abhinav Bharat was involved in various revolutionary activities including armed resistance against British officials.
 
• It drew inspiration from Italian revolutionary movements and was initially called Mitra Mela before being renamed.
 
 
 
• **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar's Imprisonment:**
 
 
• In 1909, Savarkar was arrested for his involvement in revolutionary activities and was sentenced to life imprisonment in the Andaman Islands.
 
• He spent nearly a decade in the Cellular Jail, also known as Kala Pani.
 
 
 
• **Literary Contributions:**
 
 
• While imprisoned, Savarkar wrote several influential works including "The First War of Indian Independence of 1857."
 
• His writings were instrumental in promoting revolutionary ideas and inspiring future freedom fighters.
 
 
 
• **Hindutva Ideology:**
 
 
• Post his release, Savarkar became a prominent ideologue of Hindutva, advocating for Hindu nationalism.
 
• He wrote the book "Hindutva: Who is a Hindu?" in which he outlined his vision of a Hindu nation.
